a × b = a.x·b.y − a.y·b.x > 0: b is to the left = 0: same line < 0: b is to the right
Computational geometry (计算几何) starts with vectors and two products.
The dot product a·b = axbx + ayby measures the angle (0 at right angles).
The cross product a × b = axby − aybx is twice the signed triangle area: positive when b turns left from a.

Almost every test is a cross-product sign: which side of a line a point lies on, whether two segments cross, whether a polygon turns left. Polygon area = ½ |Σ pi × pi+1| (the shoelace formula). Use integers when inputs are integers; with doubles compare against a small EPS.

Convex hull (P2742): sort points by x, build the lower chain left to right and the upper chain right to left, popping while the last turn is not to the left. O(n log n). The hull here is the triangle (4, 8), (7, 8), (4, 12): perimeter 3 + 5 + 4 = 12, area 6.
Use ≤ 0 in the pop condition to drop collinear points (or < 0 to keep them, if the problem wants them). Duplicate points and n ≤ 2 are the classic edge cases.
Sweep with a set ordered by y.

Closest pair of points (平面最近点对): sort by x and sweep. Keep a set of the points within the current best distance h to the left, ordered by y; for each new point only those with |y − yp| < h can be closer, and there are only a few of them. O(n log n).

Other classic geometry: rotating calipers on the hull for the farthest pair (P1452) and the smallest enclosing rectangle (P3187); half-plane intersection (P4196); minimum enclosing circle by random incremental construction (第15章).
P1257 / P1429. The second test has 300 random points and is checked against Python comparing all pairs.
Duplicate points: the set stores (y, x) pairs, so two equal points would collide; then the answer is 0 anyway. With such a case possible, check duplicates while sorting.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. Dot: angle; cross a × b: twice the signed area; > 0 means b turns left.
2. Area = ½ |Σ pᵢ × pᵢ₊₁|.
3. Hull: sort by x, lower then upper chain, pop while not a left turn.
4. Closest pair: sweep by x, set by y, only |dy| < h matters.
5. Integers when possible; with doubles compare using EPS.
